source_text: Quod autem Apostolum dixisse commemoras Omnes nos manifestari oportet ante tribunal Christi, ut reportet unusquisque propria corporis sui prout gessit, sive bonum, sive malum
pass_a_gloss: That/which however apostle dixisse commemoras all we manifestari it-is-necessary before tribunal of-Christ, so-that/as reportet unusquisque own of-the-body of-himself prout gessit, or good, or evil.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: We must all appear before Christ’s judgment seat, so that each may receive what belongs to his own body, according to what he has done, whether good or evil. (2 Corinthians 5:10)

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
